newsitem.title: SYRIA: Former South Yemen president to return home.
newsitem.headline: Former South Yemen president to return home.

text.p: Former South Yemen president Ali Nasser Mohammed will return to Aden on Thursday for the first time since he was ousted in a bloody 1986 coup.
Mohammed said in an interview on Wednesday at his residence in the Syrian capital that he will travel on a plane sent by Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
But the former president, who still has political influence in south Yemen, said he was not thinking now of any government post or of staying in Yemen permanently.

"I experienced authority and was burned by its fire...in the past I took the jobs of a governor, a minister, a prime minister, a vice president and a president but now my concern is is to develop the Arab Centre for Strategic Studies which I chair," he said.
"I did not discuss the issue of my participation in authority and do not think of that at present," the former president told Reuters.
Mohammed was ousted from power in South Yemen in January 1986 after bloody fighting with forces of Ali Salem al-Baidh, who signed a unity treaty with North Yemen in 1989.
But Baidh was defeated in a 1994 civil war by Saleh. Baidh and his supporters were forced to flee to Arab Gulf states and Egypt.
Yemeni sources say Mohammed, whose supporters hold senior posts in Saleh's government, could help ease tension between parties in north and south Yemen caused by the 1994 civil war.

"Things are now moving towards normalisation among the parties and the responsibility of restoring stability is not only that of the president...everybody should take part in building the country and bringing prosperity," Mohammed said.
Mohammed, who last year established the centre for Arab strategic studies with Damascus as its headquarters, said he would open a branch in the Yemeni capital Sanaa during his visit.
He said there were no plans for a branch in Aden although this might be done when financial resources were available "and in coordination with our brothers there."
The former president said he would meet Saleh and take part in celebrations for the 29th anniversary of independence and the seventh anniversary of the unity treaty between south and north Yemen.
Mohammed began his career as governor of the Yemen Islands immediately after independence from Britain in 1967. In 1969 he was named minister of local adminstration.
In 1970 he became defence minister and in 1971 prime minister. He was vice-president between 1971 and 1978. He was president from 1980 until ousted in 1986.
